items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: So you got to give Norman GranZ some credit. But I would say those three -- Norman GranZ and George Wein started his festival, the Newport Festival of 1954, and now he's presented jazz all over the world. I worked with George all over South America, Vienna, Spain, France, Holland, all over Europe --

ctx.x: So these people, these parasites who are alongside of these creative jazz players, they don't help them. They suck what money they can get out of them and the only ones who really help are people like John Hammond, because he came in with the money, and the others who have taken less money out, but have done some good. Like you have to give credit to George Wein and Norman Granz, because they have not been negative; they made money, but again, their people have made money, too.
